title: Scaling a hypercontractive variable
statement: Let $\\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set, let $X:\\Omega\\to\\mathbb R$, let $p,q\\in[0,\\infty]$, and let $\\rho,c\\in\\mathbb R$. If for every $a,b\\in\\mathbb R$ the uniform $L^q$ norm of $a+\\rho bX$ is at most the uniform $L^p$ norm of $a+bX$, then the same inequality holds with $X$ replaced by the function $x\\mapsto cX(x)$. At exponent $\\infty$, the uniform norm means the maximum absolute value on $\\Omega$.
hypotheses_covered: the stated affine norm inequality holds for all real $a,b$
